hints.S06_A1: The dash proves it: even the metal SLIDE was TOO HOT TO TOUCH, and the playground is compared to a FRYING PAN. Ask: which word describes extreme heat? The others are about cold, darkness or water.
hints.S06_A2: It appears AFTER THE RAIN, stretches ACROSS THE SKY and has SEVEN COLOURS. Ask: which of these do you see rather than hear? Thunder is a sound, and lightning is a flash - neither has colours.
hints.S06_A3: The rain has STOPPED, the air is COOL, and children are running to the PUDDLES to enjoy themselves. Ask: which phrase means to play happily in water? The other choices mean avoiding, quitting or breaking.
hints.S06_A4: Everyone is SAFE, the home is INTACT, and it feels like a MIRACLE. Ask: does the idiom describe great joy and relief, or sickness, or trouble, or sadness? An idiom cannot be read word by word.
hints.S06_A5: They already knew it was a RAINY MORNING - Mother was telling them not to forget the UMBRELLAS. Ask: which verb means to make someone remember something? 'Suggested' offers a new idea; 'discovered' finds something out.
hints.S06_B1: The subject is NOBODY, not 'the VILLAGE'. Words like nobody and everybody behave like ONE person. Ask: in the present tense, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the verb with -s?
hints.S06_B2: 'HAS' is already in the sentence, so the blank must partner with has. Ask: after has, do we use the plain verb, the -s form, the -ing form, or the past participle? Only one of them completes a present perfect.
hints.S06_B3: The children's action was already going on when the SKY SUDDENLY DARKENED and cut across it. Ask: which choice shows an action in progress in the PAST? A plain past verb only shows a finished action.
hints.S06_B4: THAN tells you the river now is being measured against the river BEFORE - just two states compared. Ask: does a short adjective take -er, or 'most'? And can you ever put 'more' in front of a word that already ends in -er?
hints.S06_B5: The second half gives the REASON why the beach was impossible: the weather was too STORMY. Ask: which joining word introduces a reason? 'So' gives a result, and 'although' would signal a contrast instead.
hints.S06_B6: A tag mirrors the main verb. The statement has no 'is' or 'are' - it uses the plain verb ARRIVES. Ask: which helping verb stands in for a plain present verb? And after a positive statement, is the tag positive or negative?
hints.S06_B7: 'EARLY YESTERDAY MORNING' is finished time, so the verb must be past. Ask: what is the past of this verb? Careful - it is irregular, so its past form looks exactly like the plain form.
hints.S06_B8: PUDDLES is plural, and they are right OUTSIDE where Mother can point at them. Ask: which word points at more than one thing that is CLOSE BY? 'That' and 'this' point at one thing only.
hints.S06_C1: 'SIX O'CLOCK' is an exact point on the clock. Ask: which preposition goes in front of clock times? Say each choice aloud before 'six o'clock' - only one sounds right.
hints.S06_C2: The tunnel was driven through while the JOURNEY was still going on - the blank covers a whole stretch of time. Ask: which preposition means 'all through a period of time'?
hints.S06_C3: A TUNNEL has an entrance at one end and an exit at the other, and the car goes in one side and out the other. Ask: which preposition shows movement from one end of something to the other?
hints.S06_C4: They reached the hotel some time before NOON, or just as noon struck - noon is the deadline. Ask: which preposition means 'not later than' a given time? The one for an exact clock time is already used in blank 1.
hints.S06_C5: 'The AFTERNOON' is a part of the day, not an exact clock time. Ask: which preposition do we use with parts of the day, like the morning or the evening?
hints.S06_C6: The jackets went on FIRST, and the VISIT came afterwards. Ask: which preposition puts one event EARLIER than another? It is the opposite of the word you need in blank 7.
hints.S06_C7: DINNER came first, and sitting by the FIRE came later. Ask: which preposition puts one event LATER than another? It is the opposite of the word needed in blank 6.
hints.S06_C8: 'SATURDAY MORNING' names a particular day. Ask: which preposition goes with days and dates - the one for exact times, the one for parts of the day, or the one for days of the week?
hints.S06_D1: It appeared on TELEVISION and WARNED of rain before a single drop had fallen. Ask: which box word names the report that tells you what the weather will do? Thunder and lightning are things you see or hear, not reports.
hints.S06_D2: They RAN UNDER THE ROOF of the bus stop to get out of the rain. Ask: which box word completes the fixed phrase 'to take ___'? You take it in order to be protected from the weather.
hints.S06_D3: WATER DRIPPED FROM THEIR HAIR - so how wet were the shirts? Ask: which box word describes something completely wet through? It is a describing word here, after 'were already'.
hints.S06_D4: It BLEW ACROSS THE FIELD and it was COOL - so it is moving air, and a gentle kind. Ask: which box word names a light wind? Thunder and lightning belong to the storm, not to the calm after it.
hints.S06_D5: The rain has stopped, but water is still lying ALONG THE PATH, so the cyclists must steer around them. Ask: which box word names small pools of water on the ground? It must be plural, because there are many.
hints.S06_E1: The underlined word means 'at this place', but the sentence is about THUNDER reaching your ears. Ask: which spelling belongs to your ears? One of them has the word EAR hidden inside it.
hints.S06_E2: FALL is an irregular verb, so -ed cannot be right. Ask: how would you say it in the past - 'yesterday the rain ___ heavily'? Irregular verbs change their shape instead of taking an ending.
hints.S06_E3: TELL is irregular too, so -ed is wrong. Ask: what is its past form - 'yesterday she ___ me a story'? It changes its vowel, exactly as sell becomes sold.
hints.S06_E4: Read the whole subject: FATHER AND I - that is two people. Ask: does a plural subject take the singular verb or the plural one? Do not match the verb to the word nearest to it.
hints.S06_E5: The GROUP CHAT belongs to the neighbours - more than one neighbour. Ask: does a plain -s show ownership, or only make a plural? Where does the apostrophe go when the owners are many?
hints.S06_F1: A yes/no question turned into REPORTED speech. Ask three things: which small joining word follows ASKED? Does the question keep its question word order, or become normal statement order? And what happens to 'will'?
hints.S06_F2: One action was already going on when the other one suddenly began. Ask: which sentence is the longer action in progress, and which is the sudden one? Put WHEN in front of the sudden one.
